Sukoon looks for patterns in your readings and logbook and compares them with published clinical targets and formulas. It doesn\'t diagnose or prescribe, it doesn\'t know your whole situation, and it can be wrong — sensors drift and logs miss things.\n\nNothing here tells you to change a dose. Any change to insulin, food or activity is your own decision and responsibility, ideally made with your diabetes team. If you feel unwell or you\'re low, treat first and get help.
OFTEN DISCUSSED WITH YOUR CARE TEAM

A new sensor: You → Sensor → Start a new sensor, then hold the phone to it; Sukoon starts it (no other app needed) and pairs it. A running one: You → Sensor → Connect sensor, then hold the top of the phone against the sensor until it buzzes. Sukoon reads its memory (the last 8 hours appear at once) and takes over its Bluetooth stream, so other apps (like DiaBox) stop getting readings; a scan in that app takes it back, and a new tap in Sukoon takes it again. “Check sensor” only reads it. Readings come every minute; saving fewer (You → Sensor → Readings) keeps history lighter, and alarms still check every one. The 24-hour note under Connection counts gaps: usually the phone was out of reach (a few metres, less through a body or a wall), or the phone paused Sukoon in the background. If the phone loses the sensor halfway through, keep it still: it carries on by itself.

The big number is your latest reading, with an arrow for where it\'s heading. A reading older than 10 minutes is greyed out and never shown as current. A new sensor needs an hour to warm up, and in its last day a banner tells you when it stops. The icons at the top log food and insulin; “u active” is rapid insulin that\'s still working. Anything a new sensor reads in its first hour shows in grey and counts for nothing (no alarms, reports or AI).

Urgent low (under 55) is always on: it takes over the screen and keeps sounding until you answer it, a minute at a time. Low (70 by default), going low, high (180 by default) and no readings are set in You → Alarms & sounds; each has Sukoon\'s own sound (Rise, Ripple, Drift, Warm, Knock), or a phone sound or your own file. While a low sounds, the alarm volume is lifted and put back after. “See and hear each alarm” plays any of them. “Can alarms reach you?” lists anything stopping them, with a fix for each; “What your alarms did” shows every alarm, what got through and how it was answered.

If an urgent low, or a lost signal while you were low, gets no answer for the time you choose (10 minutes by default), Sukoon counts down 60 seconds on screen, then texts everyone in You → People → Emergency contacts and calls the first one; again after 30 minutes if there\'s still no answer, and a “back to normal” text once you\'re 70 or more. Any answer, even swiping the alarm away, restarts the clock; “I\'m OK” stops it. On Now, “Alert my emergency contact” texts, WhatsApps or calls them yourself.

Trends → Logbook holds meals, rapid and basal insulin, finger-pricks, activity and notes. A meal can carry the insulin you took for it and how many minutes before eating. Each entry shows your glucose at that moment; a finger-prick shows how far the sensor was from your meter. The AI can estimate a meal\'s carbs from a photo or a description, but it never suggests doses.

The graph shows any range from 3 hours to 14 days, with time in range and GMI (an A1C estimate), and every reading listed below it. Insights finds patterns, like recurring lows at a certain hour, and says where each rule comes from; nothing there is an instruction. Report gives the one-page AGP summary clinics use, with a PDF to share.

You → Appearance → Make a widget: pick a style (Number, Number + graph, Graph, Ring, Today, Insulin, Following), a size, what it shows and its background, and the preview is the real widget with your numbers. “Add to home screen” places it at that size. Long-press a widget to edit it. An old reading greys out, never shown as current.

You → People → Sharing: make an account, then “Invite someone to follow you” makes a one-time code (24 hours); Send shares it with the follower page link. On Android they enter it in Sukoon; on an iPhone or any phone they open khairyky.github.io/sukoon, add it to the home screen and enter it there (alarms sound there only while it\'s open). Only real readings are shared, never demo data. Either side can end a follow. “Alarms your followers get” picks which of your alarms sound on their phones; urgent low always does. With a parent lock on, changing that, sharing, removing a follower, signing out or deleting the account needs the PIN.

Nightscout (You → Apps & data): readings and logbook go to your own site. AI assistant: your free Gemini key; asking a question or estimating a meal sends a summary of your readings and logbook (or the photo) to Google, and it never suggests doses. Reports: CSV export, and Backup (below).

Off by default, because the sensor\'s factory calibration is usually best. When on (You → Sensor), Sukoon nudges readings toward up to 4 finger-pricks from the last 7 days taken while your glucose was steady, within ±20 mg/dL and ×0.8–1.25, and it never raises a low reading.

Sukoon keeps a small notification with your glucose; that keeps it running. Allow everything in You → Help & about → Setup check, and on Samsung or Xiaomi set Sukoon to Unrestricted / Never sleeping. If the phone stops Sukoon anyway, a watchdog wakes it and the no-readings alarm sounds. After a restart or an update it reconnects by itself (a minute or two).

Sukoon is not a medical device. If a reading doesn\'t match how you feel, check with a finger-prick, and follow your care team\'s advice on treatment. In an emergency, call your local emergency number.

LibreLinkUp (You → People): sign in with a LibreLinkUp account and everyone sharing with it from Abbott\'s Libre app (Libre 2, 3 and Plus, Android or iPhone) is followed here, with their alarms. In their Libre app: Connected apps → LibreLinkUp → add your email. Dexcom (You → People): a Dexcom wearer\'s login, with Share on in their Dexcom app (G6, G7, ONE). Either can also be your own glucose: You → Sensor. Both come through the internet, a minute (LibreLinkUp) or five (Dexcom) behind the sensor, and use those companies\' own apps\' connections, which they can change.

Pull down on Now or the Logbook to bring the latest in; You → Apps & data → Resync reads the last 7 days again and says how many MyFitnessPal meals Health Connect has. If that\'s none, MyFitnessPal isn\'t sharing: update it and connect again. Workouts of 10 minutes or more, steps and water come in the same way.

You → Insulin & logbook → Reminder: at your time each day, if no long-acting was logged in the 12 hours before, a notification comes. “Took it” logs your last amount; “In 30 min” waits. It comes back every 30 minutes, 3 times, and goes away as soon as the dose is logged anywhere. The Insulin widget has “Took it” too.

You → Reports → Back up everything saves one file with your readings, logbook, settings, sensor pairing and meal photos; keep it somewhere safe, it\'s private. Restore puts it all back on this or a new phone: Sukoon closes and opens as it was. Home-screen widgets need adding again.
This version uses Sukoon\'s new signature, so Android needs a reinstall: back up everything, uninstall Sukoon, install it, then restore.
